method.selection_policy: LLM-selected market-relevant items from news_digest.json; preserves source metadata and excludes noise.

framework.Equities: Broad equity/risk sentiment; market-moving mega-cap/AI allowed; low-signal single-stock noise excluded.
framework.Commodities: Physical commodity futures framework; supply disruption/demand strength positive; supply increase/demand weakness negative.
framework.FX: USD-centric basket; non-USD currency strength positive; USD/DXY strength negative.
framework.Rates: Bond-price framework; yields up/selloff/higher-for-longer negative; yields down/bond rally/cooler inflation positive.

Equities.title: The AI trade cooled and oil sank. A closer look at Wall Street's volatile week
Equities.summary: Micron finished the week in the red despite a blockbuster earnings report. But falling oil prices was good news for the fight against inflation.
Equities.reason: Captures the dominant near-term equity narrative: cooling AI-led rally and sector rotation. Oil falling helps inflation narrative but tech-led weakness is the primary market impulse, so net negative for risk/tech.

Equities.title: SpaceX set to join Nasdaq 100, paving way for wave of passive buying
Equities.reason: Index inclusion implies meaningful passive demand and reweights for tech/Growth-heavy benchmarks — a notable pro-equity liquidity/flow driver, especially for Nasdaq-linked products.

Equities.title: Trump admin allows Anthropic to release Mythos AI model to some companies, government agencies
Equities.summary: Anthropic disabled access to its Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models to comply with a government export control directive citing "national security authorities."
Equities.reason: Eases some regulatory uncertainty around advanced models by permitting limited commercial/government access — modestly positive for AI adoption and AI-sector sentiment.

Equities.title: AI Rout Exposes Wall Street’s $270 Billion Speculation Machine
Equities.reason: Frames a large, market-wide unwind of AI-driven speculative positioning — high-impact negative for risk appetite and a key driver of recent index volatility and derisking flows.

Equities.title: S&P 500 ends lower; chips tumble and Moderna rallies
Equities.reason: Concrete market action: index-level weakness led by chip selloff reinforces the narrative of AI/semiconductor volatility and contributes to broader risk-off dynamics.

Equities.title: BIS says debt, AI boom and fragilities raise global risks
Equities.reason: Official warning from BIS amplifies macro/regime risk around leverage and AI-driven investment bubbles — supports a more cautious market regime and downside risk to equities.

Equities.title: Rise in memory chip costs puts pressure on retailers of laptops and smartphones
Equities.summary: As the global race for AI moves forward, a shortage of memory chips has begun to drive up prices of consumer electronics and may lead to product shortages.
Equities.reason: Supply-driven cost pressure threatens margins and could feed into weaker consumer tech demand or higher prices — a modest headwind for parts of the market tied to consumer electronics.

Rates.title: Fed’s Kashkari: “I have one rate hike penciled in for 2026”
Rates.summary: Federal Reserve (Fed) Bank of Minneapolis President Neel Kashkari said during a panel discussion at the Aspen Ideas Festival 2026 in Aspen, Colorado, that he remains concerned about inflation in the service sector, while also noting some signs of improvement i
Rates.reason: A Fed regional president flagging an additional hike raises probability of higher-for-longer policy and is directly negative for bond prices (yields higher). High relevance because it shapes US policy expectations.

Rates.title: Supreme Court ruling, ECB conference likely to further frame Fed chief Warsh's early tenure
Rates.reason: Political and international events that could influence the framing of the Fed chair's early policy path. Small negative tilt for bonds as political/legal uncertainty and external scrutiny can complicate Fed communications and market pricing.

Rates.title: ECB to integrate non-financial credit claim portfolios into general collateral framework, phasing out temporary measures
Rates.reason: Phasing out temporary collateral measures and integrating non-financial credit claims into the GC framework signals normalization in ECB market operations, likely reducing liquidity/backstops and putting upward pressure on euro-area yields (negative for bond prices).

Rates.title: Asset Purchase Facility: Gilt Sales – Market Notice 19 June 2026
Rates.summary: This Market Notice sets out the schedule for sales in Q3 2026 of gilts held in the Asset Purchase Facility (APF) for monetary policy purposes.
Rates.reason: Planned gilt sales from the APF increase net supply and remove central-bank balance-sheet support for the gilt market — a clear negative impulse for gilt prices (yields higher) with high relevance to UK rates.

Rates.title: Bank Rate maintained at 3.75% - June 2026 Monetary Policy Summary and Minutes
Rates.summary: The Bank of England’s Monetary Policy Committee is responsible for making decisions about Bank Rate.
Rates.reason: The BoE holding Bank Rate at a restrictive level implies less chance of near-term easing and supports a higher-for-longer gilt yield narrative — modestly negative for bond prices.

Rates.title: Why investors may want to prioritize bond markets outside the U.S.
Rates.summary: Allspring Global Investments is pushing clients toward countries with central banks that are raising interest rates or have different inflation dynamics.
Rates.reason: Flows shifting toward non-US bond markets imply relative selling pressure on US Treasuries and higher US yields. Relevant for cross-border demand dynamics in global rates markets.

Rates.title: Trading in these two ETFs suggests inflation fears are overblown
Rates.summary: It could have been a big week for bond bears, if it weren't for crude oil.
Rates.reason: ETF flows/positioning suggesting inflation fears are easing is a modest positive for bond prices (yields lower). Treated as a lower-relevance, market-structure/flow signal.

Rates.title: South Korea: Exports and inflation support rate hike path – DBS
Rates.summary: DBS Group Research’s Ma Tieying expects South Korea’s June exports to remain very strong, with year-on-year growth around 50–60% and the trade surplus widening above USD30bn. AI-related semiconductor demand and higher memory prices are seen offsetting energy i
Rates.reason: Stronger exports and demand-driven inflation raise the likelihood of further BOK tightening — negative for Korean bond prices. Regional rates impact with moderate relevance.

Rates.title: Philippines: Stagflation risks as prices surge – HSBC
Rates.summary: HSBC strategists warn that the Philippines is flirting with stagflation, as slowing Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth coincides with the highest inflation in ASEAN. Weak public spending and cautious households are dragging demand, while the labour market sof
Rates.reason: Rising inflation risk in the Philippines increases the chance of policy tightening or risk premia on local bonds — negative for local bond prices; regional relevance only.

Rates.title: Japan: Food and services signal steady inflation – Societe Generale
Rates.summary: Societe Generale economists Reo Sakida and Jin Kenzaki analyze June Tokyo Consumer Price Index (CPI), noting that overall inflation dynamics in Japan changed little from May despite a modest upside surprise in headline and core readings.
Rates.reason: Modest upside surprise but overall steady inflation implies limited BOJ reaction in the near term; slight negative tilt for JGBs given the upside surprise but low relevance.

Rates.title: Australia: Labour market rebound masks emerging slack – UOB
Rates.summary: UOB’s Lee Sue Ann highlights that Australia’s unemployment rate dipped to 4.4% in May with a 40.3k employment gain, mainly in part-time jobs, and participation rising to 66.7%.
Rates.reason: Employment gains driven by part-time jobs and emerging slack point to softer wage/inflationary pressure, mildly supportive for Australian bonds (yields lower). Low-to-moderate relevance.

Rates.title: Bond giant Pimco flexes muscles with private placements push
Rates.summary: Firm tries to capitalise on some borrowers’ need to raise cash as boundaries with public markets blur
Rates.reason: Shift of issuance into private placements can relieve public bond supply and slightly support public bond prices; a niche market-structure signal with low relevance to sovereign rates.

FX.title: Forecasting the upcoming week: US Dollar faces labor market test as NFP takes center stage
FX.summary: The upcoming week will bring a fresh test for major currency pairs as investors look ahead to key United States (US) labor market data, ISM Manufacturing figures, Eurozone inflation releases, and central bank commentary from the Federal Reserve (Fed), European
FX.reason: NFP-centered calendar is a direct USD risk — a strong print would likely bolster the Dollar (negative for USD‑pairs). Story signals elevated USD upside risk into the print, but is principally a volatility/data event rather than a confirmed trend.

FX.title: British Pound rebounds as US Dollar rally fades, UK politics stabilize
FX.summary: The Pound Sterling (GBP) gains 0.20% against the Greenback on Friday as the latter recoils after hitting year-to-date (YTD) highs, with money markets pricing in a less hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed), despite policymakers stating they will focus on inflation.
FX.reason: Explicit GBP/USD move driven by USD profit‑taking and softer Fed pricing — clear FX transmission. Represents modest relief in non‑USD pairs after recent Dollar strength.

FX.title: ECB: Another hike before eventual cuts – Commerzbank
FX.summary: Commerzbank strategists note that despite lower Oil and gas prices, European Central Bank (ECB) officials still signal at least one more rate increase, which the bank forecasts for September.
FX.reason: Central‑bank guidance pointing to another ECB hike is supportive for EUR vs USD; rate‑path divergence is a high‑relevance FX driver and reinforces EUR upside vs Dollar.

FX.title: Euro holds ground against the US Dollar as traders weigh Middle East tensions and Fed outlook
FX.summary: EUR/USD trades on the front foot on Friday but remains on track for a second straight weekly loss as the fragile situation in the Middle East and hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) outlook keep the US Dollar's (USD) downside limited.
FX.reason: Geopolitical stress (Middle East) plus hawkish Fed commentary is supportive of the Dollar and constrains EUR gains — clear USD‑support narrative weighing on EUR/USD.

FX.title: The Japanese Yen got its hike; Tokyo still has to do the rest
FX.summary: USD/JPY ended the week pressing the 162.00 handle, a whisker beneath its multi-decade high, and the more revealing detail is what it took to drag the Yen up there: a Bank of Japan (BoJ) rate hike that was billed as the turning point.
FX.reason: BoJ hiking cycle and the marked move in USD/JPY are high‑impact FX developments. A policy turning point in Japan materially changes JPY risk/reward and supports JPY vs USD (positive for non‑USD pairs involving JPY).

FX.title: Canadian Dollar trims gains as US-Iran tensions and hawkish Fed outlook support US Dollar
FX.summary: The Canadian Dollar (CAD) trims part of its intraday gains on Friday as uncertainty surrounding a final US-Iran peace agreement and expectations of a hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) help the US Dollar (USD) recover some of its losses after coming under pressure
FX.reason: Geopolitical risk and Fed hawkishness are supporting USD, trimming CAD gains. Direct pair mention and clear USD transmission justify modest negative score for CAD vs USD.

FX.title: Australian Dollar recovers as US Dollar eases on profit-taking
FX.summary: AUD/USD is recovering near 0.6900 on Friday as the US Dollar (USD) weakens with investors taking profits ahead of the end of the semester after a two-week rally in the Greenback. The move helped the Australian Dollar (AUD) recover some intraday ground, althoug
FX.reason: AUD rebound driven by USD profit‑taking is a direct FX flow; relevant but lower‑impact and likely transient around positioning/semester‑end flows.

FX.title: Malaysian Ringgit: Policy support tempers downside but caps upside – MUFG
FX.summary: Lloyd Chan at MUFG notes the Malaysian Ringgit outperformed, rising 0.4% versus the US Dollar (USD) after Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) reintroduced a 2024-style FX support measure to encourage repatriation and conversion of offshore earnings.
FX.reason: Domestic FX support measures from BNM explicitly affect MYR flows and cap volatility — direct FX intervention/support story with localized but clear impact.

FX.title: Chinese Yuan: Weakness against US Dollar seen as corrective – OCBC
FX.summary: OCBC’s FX strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong note USD/CNH’s recent run-up has stalled, with the pair around 6.8020 and daily bullish momentum intact but RSI turning lower from overbought.
FX.reason: USD/CNH stalling suggests corrective pressure on USD vs CNH — a modest, market‑specific FX technical/flow signal rather than a regime change.

FX.title: Singapore Dollar: Gains momentum against US Dollar – OCBC
FX.summary: OCBC’s FX strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong highlight that USD/SGD has eased as US Dollar (USD) momentum softened on core Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Price Index data, with the pair around 1.2960.
FX.reason: USD softness after PCE supports SGD; explicit USD/SGD move makes this directly relevant though lower impact than central‑bank or geopolitical drivers.

FX.title: US President Trump: Iran broke the ceasefire with Hormuz drone strike
FX.summary: US President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social on Friday that Iran violated the ceasefire after launching drones at ships in the Strait of Hormuz, with one of them hitting the upper deck of a large cargo-carrying ship.
FX.reason: Geopolitical escalation in the Strait of Hormuz raises safe‑haven demand for USD and heightens oil risk premia — a material FX/market driver that supports Dollar strength and pressures risk‑linked currencies.

Commodities.title: Gold price rebounds as falling US yields weigh on US Dollar
Commodities.summary: Gold (XAU/USD) price recovers some ground on Friday, hitting a two-day high of $4,096 as the Greenback edges lower alongside Treasury yields after investors trimmed hawkish bets on the Federal Reserve (Fed). The XAU/USD pair trades at $4,076, up 1.24%.
Commodities.reason: Gold rally driven by falling US yields and weaker USD — classic positive drivers for bullion. Macro rates/FX transmission is a broad market driver for gold, so moderate-high relevance.

Commodities.title: UAE's exit from OPEC+ reduced the group's share of crude oil production and capacity
Commodities.summary: On April 28, 2026, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) announced that it was leaving OPEC, effective on May 1. OPEC was formed in 1960 by Iraq, Iran, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, and Venezuela, with the stated objective to "coordinate and unify petroleum policies among Me
Commodities.reason: Structural change to OPEC+ membership alters coordination and capacity shares — tends to increase supply-side uncertainty and potential for higher unilateral output (negative for oil prices). High thematic relevance.

Commodities.title: Permian natural gas production increased faster than crude oil
Commodities.summary: The Permian region's marketed natural gas production grew from 17.2 billion cubic feet per day (Bcf/d) in 2021 to 27.6 Bcf/d in 2025, a 60% increase, according to data from our latest Short Term Energy Outlook. Over the same period, crude oil production grew b
Commodities.reason: Large Permian gas supply growth is a clear supply-side bearish signal for US natural gas prices. It's a fundamental production trend with moderate relevance to the gas commodity complex.

Commodities.title: Renewed Strikes Threaten Setback to Shipping Recovery in Persian Gulf
Commodities.reason: Renewed strikes in the Persian Gulf threaten maritime traffic through key oil chokepoints — significant upside risk for oil and fuel markets through supply/disruption channels. High market-moving relevance.

Commodities.title: U.S. commercial crude oil inventories have decreased in June
Commodities.summary: For the week ending June 19, 2026, U.S. refineries processed 17.1 million barrels per day (b/d) of crude oil, down 81,000 b/d from the previous week, and they operated at 96.1% capacity utilization. Gasoline production averaged 9.5 million b/d, and distillate
Commodities.reason: Reported drawdown in US commercial crude stocks is a straightforward bullish fundamental for oil balances. Relevant to near-term price dynamics.

Commodities.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG breaks below $60, bears eye $55
Commodities.summary: Silver (XAG/USD) price registers gains of nearly 2% on Friday but is poised to finish the week with losses of nearly 10%, as the white metal falls below the $60.00 threshold for the first time since the rally that began at the beginning of December 2025.
Commodities.reason: Technical/price-forecast piece on silver breakdown. Price-technical items have limited relevance per framework, so relevance capped at 0.8 despite clear bearish near-term price signal.

Commodities.title: WTI Oil weakens as Middle East export recovery tempers supply risk concerns
Commodities.summary: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) US Oil falls 3.25% on Friday and trades around $69.05 at the time of writing, after hitting its lowest level since late February at $68.48 earlier in the day.
Commodities.reason: Market reaction to easing Middle East export disruptions reduces immediate risk premium — a material bearish impulse for oil with above-average relevance given region's importance.

Commodities.title: Oil prices climb in after-hours trading as U.S. makes retaliatory strike on Iran
Commodities.reason: Direct military retaliation tied to Iran elevates immediate supply risk and typically triggers prompt oil price upside. Event-driven, high-relevance market-moving item for oil.

Commodities.title: Mines will hold back Strait of Hormuz shipping for months, CEO warns
Commodities.summary: NYK’s Takaya Soga says safe routes are ‘extremely limited’, restricting traffic to half prewar levels
Commodities.reason: Persistent mining of shipping routes in the Strait of Hormuz suggests prolonged constraints on tanker flows — a sustained supply-risk narrative with strong relevance for oil markets.

Commodities.title: Tether putting $23 billion gold stockpile to work with bullion-backed loans
Commodities.reason: If Tether deploys a large gold stockpile into lending markets, it can modestly boost liquidity/utilization of physical gold — supportive for bullion but not a primary macro driver; assign low-moderate relevance.

Crypto.title: Bitcoin falls below $60,000, on track for a rare back-to-back quarterly loss
Crypto.reason: Price break below $60k and the prospect of consecutive quarterly losses highlights negative momentum and macro-driven selling pressure for crypto — clear negative for BTC and market sentiment.

Crypto.title: Federal Reserve Board requests comment on proposal to require certain payment stablecoin issuers to maintain an effective customer identification program
Crypto.summary: Federal Reserve Board requests comment on proposal to require certain payment stablecoin issuers to maintain an effective customer identification program
Crypto.reason: Fed proposal signals tighter regulatory scrutiny of payment stablecoins (KYC/CIP requirements), increasing compliance costs and regulatory uncertainty for a key crypto infrastructure subset.

Crypto.title: Binance tells EU users it will no longer provide services after failing to secure MiCA license
Crypto.reason: Major exchange losing ability to operate in the EU is a material market-structure shock — negative for liquidity and user access in a major regulatory jurisdiction.

Crypto.title: Coinbase and OKX try to lure in Binance’s EU users after it failed to secure a MiCA license
Crypto.reason: Competitive migration of EU users toward licensed exchanges represents a redistribution of flows and potential market share gains for onshore platforms — modest positive for those exchanges and for regulated access.

Crypto.title: Securitize expects to raise $400 million as tokenization firm nears public debut
Crypto.reason: Large fundraising for a tokenization platform signals institutional capital and product development in crypto infrastructure — constructive for sector growth and institutional adoption.

Crypto.title: Ethereum treasury firm Sharplink buys ether for the first time in eight months
Crypto.reason: On‑chain/treasury buying is direct demand for ETH and supports positive price pressure and signal of institutional accumulation.

Crypto.title: Polymarket hack updated to $3.1 million days after the platform promised users full refunds
Crypto.reason: Security breach and loss increases counterparty risk perceptions in DeFi/crypto platforms — negative for user trust and liquidity in decentralized markets.

Crypto.title: U.S. House Democrat, who may soon run key committee, condemns crypto in 401(k)s
Crypto.reason: Political opposition to including crypto in retirement plans highlights growing legislative/regulatory headwinds which could constrain broader retail/institutional adoption.

Crypto.title: Former Ethereum Foundation leader warns of funding gap as governance shifts
Crypto.reason: Warnings about an Ethereum funding shortfall and governance changes present medium-term ecosystem risk that could reduce development momentum and investor confidence.

Crypto.title: Japanese financial services giant SBI Holdings to buy Bitbank for $289 million
Crypto.reason: Strategic acquisition by a major financial services firm indicates ongoing institutionalization and consolidation in exchanges — modestly positive for regional market development.
